records.title: Fall Acorn Errand Route Map
records.kidDirection: Draw a fall errand route through Acorn Avenue, then write the clue that helps your hero choose the next stop.
records.adultNote: Keep the work offline and choice-based. Let the child point, draw, or label before asking for full sentences.

sections.heading: Route Stops
lines: Start at the acorn desk with this errand slip: ____________________________

sections.heading: Story Sentence
lines: My hero solves the errand mix-up by ____________________________.

records.title: Fall Seed Library Catalog Cards
records.kidDirection: Fill in three seed catalog cards with garden clues from the end of the growing season.
records.adultNote: Use this as a short observation-to-story station. The child can invent details or borrow safe details from a real garden walk.

sections.heading: Catalog Note
lines: This seed story could begin with ____________________________.

records.title: Fall Greenhouse Gear Reflection
records.kidDirection: Think like a greenhouse helper and decide how the gears should care for fall seedlings.
records.adultNote: Guide the child toward cause-and-effect language: what changed, what the hero noticed, and what small fix comes next.

sections.heading: What Changed
lines: The gear pattern surprises the hero by ____________________________

sections.heading: Reflection Sentence
lines: One clearer detail I can add to my story is ____________________________.

records.title: Winter Teacup Forecast Worksheet
records.kidDirection: Write a tiny winter forecast so Teacup Town can plan its cozy errands.
records.adultNote: Read the headings aloud and ask for short, concrete details. Keep the session adult-guided and printable-first.

sections.heading: Town Errands
lines: The picnic cart changes its plan by ____________________________.

records.title: Winter Button Bakery Crumb Map
records.kidDirection: Turn the upside-down crumb map into clear winter directions for a bakery delivery.
records.adultNote: Have the child trace the route with a finger first, then write only the labels needed to make the directions understandable.

sections.heading: Bakery Start
lines: My hero carries this warm roll: ____________________________
The first crumb clue is beside: ____________________________

sections.heading: Delivery Ending
lines: The baker thanks the hero for ____________________________.

records.title: Winter Clue Label Museum Prompt
records.kidDirection: Write museum labels that help visitors notice one useful winter clue at a time.
records.adultNote: This page is for concise explanatory writing. Encourage one clear sentence before adding extra description.

sections.heading: Curator Choice
lines: The label should leave out ____________________________ so visitors notice ____________________________.

sections.heading: Short Story Prompt
lines: When the winter museum opens, my hero notices ____________________________.
A visitor understands the clue after ____________________________.
